statements.formal_part: upper bound: Descartes independence of the b_i and of the b_i ⊗ b_i, and the vanishing of the coefficients c_ij in one group and between two groups. Lower bound, for points in general position: the map M ≠ 0 with M a_i ∈ ⟨b_i⟩ (dimension count), M has rank 4, and the pulled-back Plücker form is a nonzero symmetric form vanishing on simple tensors with every a_i ⊗ b_i in its radical. Not formalized: the passage from radical conditions to the relations c_ij, that general points compute qp (BSSV Lemma 3.3) and the identification of these forms with 𝒟

statements.formal_part: the mixed component: propagation along the cyclic graph on Z/n kills every c_ijh from the vertex equations (mixto); the extraction of the coefficients of t^p over the n-th roots of unity; the internal 3 × 3 component. Not formalized: the reduction to blocks and the splitting of ⋀²A*, the factorization M^ij = (a_i × a_j) ⊗ v_ij, the derivation of (mixto) from the radical conditions, and the Zariski-open passage to rational points

statements.formal_part: the uniqueness step: two PSD Gram matrices differing by an element of 𝒟, vanishing at points where the radical map is injective, coincide; the Gram matrix of Σ c_j u_j² (c_j > 0, u_j killing the points) is PSD, kills the points and has rank e. Uses Mathlib Matrix.PosSemidef.dotProduct_mulVec_zero_iff. Not formalized: that 𝒟 is the space of Segre relations and the existence of the points
